question: How to think about applying a SOX ICFR control mindset to practical AI usage within an organization, such as a Finance function

sources.name: COSO, Achieving Effective Internal Control Over Generative AI (Feb 2026)
sources.why: The standard-setter's own answer to the question: adapts the 17 COSO principles to generative AI instead of a separate framework, treats AI output as assertions needing evidence, and asks for preventive, detective and corrective controls.
match: achieving effective internal control over generative ai

sources.name: PCAOB staff Spotlight on generative AI (Jul 2024)
sources.why: The only regulator view on how preparers and auditors use GenAI: augment not replace, same diligence in review, black-box and inconsistent output limit reperformance.

sources.name: NIST AI RMF 1.0 (AI 100-1) and Generative AI Profile (AI 600-1)
sources.why: The main AI-specific framework, the writer's own 'better framework' objection; defines automation bias and warns that confabulated citations mislead reviewers.

sources.name: Peer-reviewed research on automation bias (e.g. Parasuraman & Manzey 2010)
sources.why: Evidence that a human in the loop can rubber-stamp automated output, which tests the writer's human-in-the-loop point head on.

sources.name: Fed/OCC/FDIC SR 26-2 on model risk management (Apr 2026)
sources.why: Replaced SR 11-7 and says generative and agentic AI are outside its scope, which bears directly on whether model-risk practice covers GenAI in finance.

sources.name: CAQ, Audit Committee Oversight in the Age of GenAI (2024)
sources.why: What the audit committee, the CFO office's overseer, is told to ask about GenAI in financial reporting.

sources.name: COSO, Realize the Full Potential of Artificial Intelligence (2021)
sources.why: COSO's enterprise-risk view of AI, which covers the operational decisions the writer wants in scope beyond financial reporting.
match: realize the full potential of artificial intelligence

sources.name: IIA Artificial Intelligence Auditing Framework (2024)
sources.why: Internal audit's view; useful on SDLC, change management and segregation of duties, but generic for a CFO-office reader.

sources.name: Reason, Human error: models and management (BMJ 2000)
sources.why: The origin of the Swiss cheese model the writer uses for preventive and detective layers.

sources.name: SR 11-7 Supervisory Guidance on Model Risk Management (2011), rescinded Apr 2026
sources.why: Rescinded and replaced by SR 26-2; citing it as current guidance is an error.
